Fill in missing photos in the background on any network

Choose where these lyrics will be kept
A separate file, next to the song. Doesn\'t touch the music.
In the file\'s tags. The lyrics travel with the music to any player.

It will be uploaded to OneDrive, next to the song.
You\'ll be asked for write permission on OneDrive.

Download the song to write inside it.
Android doesn\'t allow creating files next to your music when scanning the whole device. Choose a folder for lyrics in Settings, or use folder mode.
It will be saved in “%1$s”, not next to the song: Android doesn\'t allow that when scanning the whole device. Other players won\'t find it there.

No permission to modify the file
You need Wi‑Fi to upload the song
Without write permission the lyrics can\'t be saved to OneDrive
To keep the lyrics next to your song, Microsoft asks for write permission on your OneDrive. It\'s the only permission that allows it: there is no folder-scoped one.
Only for “all the music on this device” mode: Android doesn\'t allow creating the .lrc files next to your music, so they are kept here mirroring their subfolders. Folder mode doesn\'t need this.
32-bit float processing. While it\'s on, the DSP battery saver (offload) is disabled.
Mild clipping: may distort at high volume
Strong clipping: lower this boost or turn on the limiter
Will clip unless you turn the volume down.
The limiter will keep it from clipping by pulling peaks down.
Over Bluetooth the headphones usually control the volume, so turning it down here gives no headroom. Turn on the limiter or lower the preamp.
Pulls down peaks above the threshold. At 0 dB it only prevents clipping; lower, it compresses.
Adds brightness up top with gentle saturation.
Saves the whole current sound: the curve, the boosters, the preamp and the limiter.
“%1$s” is currently applied. Update it with the current sound, or save a new one?
A profile named “%1$s” already exists. Overwrite it with the current sound?
Do you have a system equalizer on?
If a system or manufacturer equalizer is active (Xiaomi, Wavelet, etc.), it will be applied along with the app\'s one and the sound will be equalized twice. We recommend using only one.
If you adjust the system equalizer while the app\'s one is on, both will apply at once and the sound will be equalized twice. You can turn off the app\'s one before opening the system one.
The player\'s equalizer button opens the system panel (MIUI/manufacturer) instead of the built-in equalizer. Turning this on switches off the built-in one.
Choose which ones show up in the picker

A preset saves the band curve only; a profile also saves the boosters, the preamp and the limiter. Hidden ones are not listed in the equalizer, but they are not deleted: you can bring them back whenever you want.
Navigation style, where the tabs go and which ones show up.
Replaces the tabs with three destinations: Home, Library and Playlists. Categories (songs, artists, albums, genres) open from Library. While this is on, tabs cannot be reordered or hidden.
Drag to reorder. Disabled tabs do not show up in the library.
At least one tab must stay on
Show the tabs in a bottom bar instead of under the search field. In landscape they always move to the side.
Shows the technical details in the player chip (FLAC · 16 bit · 44.1 kHz). You can also toggle it by tapping the chip.
Drag to reorder. Enabled actions show up in the bar; the rest go to the menu (⋮).
Swiping and tapping in the player
Evens out perceived loudness across songs using the file\'s ReplayGain tags. It only attenuates, never boosts.
No leveling: every song plays at its original loudness.
Levels track by track. Ideal for shuffling across artists.
Uses the album gain: keeps the loudness balance between tracks of the same record.
Starting level. Raise it if the music is too quiet (careful: raising it too much clamps the factor to 1.0 and loses leveling on the loudest songs).
Scans a folder on the device (subfolders included). Its songs join the same library as OneDrive.
Its songs will leave your library. The files are NOT deleted from your device.
This is your only folder: your device music will leave the library. The files are NOT deleted.
This is your only music source. To stop scanning this folder, switch to scanning the whole device, or cancel to keep it.
Scanning all music on your device…
Let\'s start with the music already on your phone. Pick either way, or skip it if all your music lives in the cloud.
Pick a provider and connect to play your cloud music and download it for offline listening.
Connect to continue; otherwise go back and choose folders.
Your cloud music is downloaded to the phone so you can listen offline. Decide how much space it can use; you can change it anytime in Settings.
Siku asks for a single one, and only for what you see here.
Play, next and the album art on your status bar and lock screen.
How much is left of the scan and of your OneDrive downloads.
You will never get promotional alerts. You can change this any time in your system settings.
Streaming and downloads from your Microsoft account.
Pick the OneDrive folder where your music lives. Its subfolders are included.
OneDrive will be scanned again from scratch. Songs outside the new folder will be removed from your library, along with their history and colors, and will leave any playlists they were in.
Read-only access: lyrics can\'t be saved here.
All the music stored on your phone, no folders to pick.
Scanning all music on your device
Add a music folder before turning off the full scan, so you\'re not left with an empty library.
To scan all the music on your device, Siku needs permission to read your audio files. You can grant it from the app settings, or pick specific folders instead (that needs no permission).
All the music on your device, or just the folders you pick.
Full scan of every source and cleanup of songs that no longer exist.
Choose which folders the device scan ignores.

The device scan indexes every piece of music the system can see, which includes messaging audio, voice recordings and game sounds. Turn off the folders that aren\'t your library. Excluded songs leave the app — along with their playlists and history — but the files are untouched.
The system sees no music on this device.
Import an .m3u from another player, or save one of your playlists to one. The file stores file paths, so it only works where that music exists.
Saves your playlists and favorites in the app folder on OneDrive so you can restore them on another device. Restoring never deletes anything: it only adds what\'s missing.
Uploads your playlists to OneDrive and replaces the previous backup.
Fetches the OneDrive backup and merges it with your current playlists.
There is no backup on OneDrive yet
Reconnect OneDrive: the backup needs a new permission
OneDrive songs and the downloaded files will be deleted. Your local music, playlists and favorites are kept; the songs come back to your playlists when you reconnect the account.
Forces a re-analysis of the album art with the new color algorithm.
All album art will be analyzed again. Any colors you picked manually will be lost and cannot be recovered.
From the artwork color down to the app background.
A single theme tone, also tinted by the artwork.
Uses the animated Material 3 wave in the player. The mini player keeps the thin bar.
Mode (flat or wavy), handle and thickness, with live preview.
Applies to both the flat and the wavy player bar.
Keeps the position handle always visible on the player bar. Turn it off and it only shows while you drag.
Uses rounded corners on the floating bar instead of the pill shape.
A circle instead of the rounded square shape on the floating bar.
Swipe the album art to change songs or down to close the player. On the mini player, swipe up to open it and down to stop playback. Double tap the sides of the album art to skip %1$d seconds.
The system theme one (wallpaper colors). Moderate and consistent across all artwork.
Color at full blast, like the media controls in the notification shade. It can overdo muted album art.
Intensity follows the cover; more neutral surfaces.
Like the previous one, with complementary accents.
Nearly gray, with a minimal hint of the album.
The accent follows the cover, but backgrounds shift to the complementary hue.
A simplified screen for continuous playback.
